section.sectionSummaryBrief: Regarding the spirit of folly, a Jew who transgresses God's will is certainly no worse than a gentile who does so.
section.t: [And regarding the spirit of folly etc. – certainly a Jewish person who transgresses His will is no worse than a gentile who transgresses His will.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Gentiles are on a lower level than Jews, yet the spirit of folly can cause them to deny God entirely, unlike Jews where it only conceals the Divine soul's wisdom.
section.t: And on the contrary: gentiles are on a lower level than the Children of Israel
(although from this perspective they are not worse)
– for with them, the spirit of folly can cover and conceal even the matter of "they call Him God of gods,"
so that they deny the existence of God entirely,
and not like with the Children of Israel,
for the spirit of folly of the kelipah "clothes the Divine soul up to the level of its wisdom,
but not including it,
because of the light of God that is clothed in wisdom"
(Tanya, chapter 24),
unlike gentiles,
who do not possess the level of wisdom of the Divine soul].

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The Tanya states that a transgressing Jew is far worse than the sitra achra and impure animals, but not worse than gentiles, since gentiles also have the spirit of folly to transgress.
section.t: Therefore: the language in Tanya chapter 24 is that "a person who transgresses His will is much worse and lower than the sitra achra and kelipah...
and more than all the things that flow from it in this world, which are impure beasts, animals, impure birds, creeping things, and reptiles,"
and it is not said that he is worse than gentiles – because,
from the aspect of the spirit of folly, even gentiles can transgress His will,
and only the sitra achra and kelipah and all the impure animals that flow from it,
for whom the matter of the spirit of folly does not apply,
cannot transgress His will at all
(and the example of this is specifically from the fact that "no harmful beast rules over a person etc.,"
for it is impossible to be otherwise).
